## Intent
Hypothesis: fusing the render scatter into the per-particle step eliminates intermediate storage and can approach the streaming ceiling despite byte-granular framebuffer writes.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill at N≈963 falls below the measured range (smallest N=10000), so it is not directly observable. The L2 spill at N≈61680 sits between N=10000 and N=100000. At death_q=0.01, ns/p decreases modestly from 8.127 (N=10000) to 7.418 (N=10000000) — a 9% drop with no knee at the L2→DRAM transition, consistent with small-N overhead amortization rather than cache-driven shape. At death_q=0.5 the curve is flat: 13.281 → 13.448, even rising slightly across the spill. Death rate raises the floor (from ~7.4 ns/p at q=0.01 to ~13.4 at q=0.5) without changing the N-shape, confirming the cost is not cache-residence-driven but branch/respawn-driven.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 9.17 GB/s at N=10000000, death_q=0.01 — 31% of the 29.9 GB/s streaming ceiling. At death_q=0.5 it falls to 5.06 GB/s (17% of ceiling). The algo is never bandwidth-bound: at q=0.01 the profile is compute-dominated (71.2% compute, 26.5% backend stall, 2.2% branch flush), while at q=0.5 it becomes branch-bound (55.8% compute, 11.6% backend, 32.3% branch flush). The transition is driven entirely by death rate, not by N — bandwidth stays flat across all N within each death-rate series. The algo never approaches the streaming ceiling in any regime.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized the per-particle physics across components, not across particles: `ldr q1, [x26]` loads four position floats, `ext.16b v3, v1, v2, #0xc` rearranges them, `fmul.4s v0, v3, v4` and `fadd.4s v0, v1, v0` apply 4-wide SIMD, and `ld1.s {v2}[1], [x8]` is an indexed single-lane load (a gather) for a velocity component. The render scatter, however, is entirely scalar: `ldrb w16, [x15]`, `add w16, w16, w8`, `csel w16, w16, w24, lo`, `strb w16, [x15]` — repeated for R, G, B at each pixel. The 19 `strb` and 12 `ldrb` instructions in the histogram are all framebuffer byte-granular read-modify-writes. These scalar byte stores explain why bandwidth caps at 31% of ceiling: the fused scatter cannot stream, and the per-particle SIMD update is dwarfed by the scalar render path.

## Verdict
Refuted — the fused scatter's byte-granular framebuffer writes cannot stream, capping achieved bandwidth at 9.17 GB/s (31% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling) even at the lowest death rate, and collapsing to 5.06 GB/s (17%) at q=0.5 where branch flush reaches 32.3% of cycles. The hypothesis that fusing eliminates intermediate storage and approaches the streaming ceiling fails because the scatter's `strb`/`ldrb` read-modify-write path dominates regardless of death rate or N.
